title: Code Heuristic Check
description: Flag keyword patterns, long lines, and delimiter counts for manual review. This heuristic check does not compile code or certify it as secure.
intro: Code Heuristic Check flags a small set of text patterns: dynamic evaluation, loose equality, maintenance markers, possible credentials, long lines, and mismatched delimiter counts. It does not compile the program or inspect all security risks. Review each reported match in context and use the project tooling for correctness checks.
audience: Developers performing a preliminary manual review of short source excerpts
input: A focused source snippet to scan for the listed text patterns, with a language label for the resulting report.
outcome: A text report listing matching lines and delimiter-count warnings, or stating that no built-in heuristic pattern matched.
review: False positives and false negatives are expected from text rules. Verify findings manually and rely on compiler, linter, and security tooling for deeper checks.
bestFor: A quick preliminary scan of a small snippet before a normal code review, without treating a clean result as a correctness or safety guarantee.
steps: Choose the language label and paste the source excerpt.
Choose Run Heuristic Check to apply the built-in text rules.
Inspect each flagged line in the original context.
Run the project compiler, tests, linter, and relevant security checks separately.
useCases: Spotting an eval call for closer manual review.
Finding TODO or FIXME markers in a pasted excerpt.
Noticing long lines before editing a documentation example.
Checking delimiter counts as a preliminary signal for malformed snippets.
commonMistakes: Calling a no-match result proof that code is secure.
Treating delimiter counts as actual syntax validation.
Automatically changing every flagged line without reading its context.
tips: Text inside literals and comments may trigger a rule.
A rule match is a review lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
Use real secrets only in approved local tooling, never in sample fixtures.
Keep test and compiler results alongside any heuristic report.

faq.question: Is this a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It scans a limited list of text patterns and cannot establish that source code is secure.

faq.question: Does a clean report mean that code compiles?
faq.answer: No. A no-match result only means that the built-in patterns did not produce a warning.

faq.question: Why can a quoted string trigger a warning?
faq.answer: The scanner reads text patterns without building a full language-specific syntax tree. Inspect each match manually.

faq.question: Does the checker execute my code?
faq.answer: No. It examines the input as text in the browser and does not call a runtime service.

faq.question: Which checks should follow this scan?
faq.answer: Use the compiler or interpreter, automated tests, a language-specific linter, and the security checks appropriate to the application.

examples.title: Dynamic evaluation warning
examples.description: Language label: JavaScript. The eval pattern is a reason for manual review; the checker does not execute this input.

- Risky dynamic execution
- Loose equality and declaration style
